To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HPV virus can be involved in SCC in immunocompetent hosts; (2) the association between HPV, CMV and HSV may be a possible factor in the development of cutaneous SCCs; (3) the interaction between CMV and HPV is a possible explanation for multiple SCC of fingers; (4) a preventive treatment by Tazarotine is a useful treatment to avoid recurrence of multiple SCC of fingers.
we describe an unusual case of multiple and diffuse SCC of fingers occurring in a patient with HIV infection and treated by total body electron beam radiation.

1) HPV is identified in SCC of fingers in an immunocompromised patient, 2) the association of HPV with other viruses (CMV, HSV) is possible and 3) the treatment by retinoids is an option in order to avoid SCC recurrence.

the study of the association of CMV, HSV, HPV and multiple SCC in an immunocompromised patient.

the patient presented a multiple SCCs of the fingers, with HPV DNA in tumoral and epidermal cells and a history of HSV and CMV infection.
HPV is not only a virus that is involved in the development of cervical cancer, but it also seems to be implicated in the development of non-melanoma cutaneous cancers in immunosuppressed patients.

the association between HPV and cutaneous carcinogenesis is not well known and that the association between cutaneous HPV and multiple SCCs of the hands in an immunocompromised patient is a rare association.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPV is a common infection of the skin and that it may be involved in some cases of SCC in immunocompromised patients, especially in the case of multiple SCCs.
the association of HPV and CMV in the development of cutaneous malignancies has been reported in the literature but not with HSV.

HPV and HSV are involved in the development of cutaneous SCC in immunocompetent individuals, and that the interaction between these viruses and CMV could explain the development of multiple cutaneous SCCs in the fingers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the identification of HPV in the epidermal cells of the tumour and in the epipidermal layer above the tumour, in the context of immunosuppression, is an argument in favour of the role of HPV in the development and the evolution of multiple SCCs in the context of a severe immunosuppression.
the presence of multiple SCCs should lead to a search for an underlying viral aetiology, and that the presence of a viral aetiology may be a marker for poor prognosis.
the association of CMV, HSV, HPV, and UV radiation may play a role in the development of a multiple SCC in an immunocompromised patient.
